items.title: George Guesnon Interview
items.q: When she came to work early at night... That was the rules we had.

ctx.x: well Bill I said this I love music and if I had my life to live over again I wouldn't be nothing else but a musician but not a badger player I'd be a trumpet player this time I better be you see cause everybody the bad you see I read in a little book kid Thomas with his enormous power he can play for 14 hours without stopping yeah but he don't play seven notes in them 14 hours either he said…

I was going to ask a little bit more. Wait a minute. Can you tell us a little about Wilhelmina Barth? Because I never did get to hear her. I know she was a good pianist. What style did she play? What kind of piano?

Well, like I told you, Bill, on a Jitney dance, you see the styles varied. When she came to work early at night, she might have played like pad of whiskey, like you say. But as the hours started to go, she was finally wide up playing like stormy weather, you know, just sitting up there caught in the wind. Because as I told you, the man used to wake us like mules. Don't let the echo of the first piece die out before you pick up another one. That was the rules we had. What size lady? Was she big and strong? Oh,…
